You'll report to the VP of Brand and work across the whole function: brand, editorial, design, product marketing, demand generation, and integrated marketing.\n\nThis is not a strategy-only role, and it isn't a glorified project-management seat either. In any given quarter the org is shipping product launches, field events, partner campaigns, and demand programs in parallel, often across regions and time zones. That pace is the reason the role exists. Your job is to make sure the right work wins when everything feels urgent, that plans turn into shipped work, and that the VP of Brand and the leadership team spend their time leading instead of firefighting.\n\nBe clear-eyed about the shape of the work. A lot of it is operational: the planning calendar, the budget, the headcount plan, the weekly business reviews, the cross-functional handoffs that break when nobody owns them. The grind is the job. You should want that part, not tolerate it.\n\nOne boundary worth naming up front. Marketing Ops owns the systems: the MarTech stack, attribution, scoring, routing, data pipelines, and the reporting everyone runs on. You'll be the heaviest consumer of that work, not the owner of it. If you find yourself rebuilding dashboards or running a tooling migration, something has gone wrong. Your seat is the operating rhythm of the org: meetings, priorities, plans, and the decisions that come out of them.\n\n\n\nWHO YOU ARE\n\nYou've run operations inside a fast, high-output B2B marketing org, and you've left it running better than you found it. You know the specific failure mode of a team that's shipping a lot and losing the thread, and you know how to pull it back without slowing everyone down.\n\nYou understand how marketing actually works, at the level of someone who's done it rather than managed it from a distance. You can talk credibly about how a campaign turns into pipeline, what account-based marketing demands from both sales and marketing before it works, and where demand-gen motions usually break. You don't have to have run every program yourself. You do have to understand them well enough that the people who run them respect your judgment.\n\nYou're fluent in the numbers. Pipeline math, funnel conversion, budget-to-impact. You can read a marketing dashboard and tell what's real from what's been dressed up, and you say so. Building the reporting is Marketing Ops' job. Yours is to use it well and push back when it doesn't add up.\n\nYou hold strategy and execution in the same hand. You can sit in a planning conversation with the VP in the morning and chase down a stuck deliverable in the afternoon, and you don't think the second thing is beneath you.\n\nYou write clearly and you communicate straight. People trust your readouts because they're honest, not because they're polished. When something is off track, you name it early.\n\nYou stay calm when it's messy. A marketing org this active will hand you ambiguity every day. Your job is to turn it into a plan other people can actually follow.\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL OWN\n\n\n\nOPERATING RHYTHM AND PLANNING\n\nRun the marketing org's planning cadence: annual and quarterly planning, goal-setting, and the weekly and monthly business reviews. Hold the calendar.\n\nDrive budget and headcount planning against the slate, working from Marketing Ops' tracking and reporting, and keep both honest as priorities shift mid-quarter. You own the trade-off conversations; Marketing Ops owns the numbers underneath them.\n\nMake the reviews worth holding. Drive the prep, the follow-through, and the decisions that should come out of them.\n\n\nPRIORITIES AND CROSS-FUNCTIONAL FLOW\n\nTurn the VP of Brand's priorities into plans the team can execute, then hold the line on those priorities when new fires start.\n\nKeep major programs from colliding or stalling across brand, editorial, design, product marketing, demand gen, and integrated marketing. A lot of this is seeing the crash coming and preventing it.\n\nBe the person teams come to when it isn't clear who owns a decision.\n\n\nCONNECTIVE TISSUE WITH THE REST OF THE COMPANY\n\nRepresent marketing in cross-functional planning with sales, product, and finance, so the org's commitments are realistic and its dependencies are visible. When marketing promises something to another team, you make sure the promise was sane and gets kept.\n\nThe systems plumbing behind that (lead routing, scoring, pipeline data) sits with Marketing Ops and RevOps. Your job is the planning and accountability layer on top of it. You'll also chase procurement and legal when purchases and projects stall.\n\n\nLEADERSHIP LEVERAGE\n\nBuild the materials leadership relies on: board updates, all-hands content, exec readouts. Make them clear and honest, not decorative.\n\nGive the VP of Brand back time and attention by carrying the work that doesn't need to land on their desk.\n\n\nSPECIAL PROJECTS\n\nLead the things that don't fit neatly on any one team's plate: a reorg, a new agency relationship, a flagship event, an org-wide planning week. Own them end to end.\n\n\n\nHOW SUCCESS WILL BE MEASURED\n\nPlanning happens on time and means something. The slate is set, owned, and funded, and people can point to it.\n\nPrograms ship on cadence without running into each other. Fewer last-minute scrambles, fewer dropped handoffs.\n\nLeadership gets time back. The VP of Brand spends more of their week on the calls that need them and less on the ones that don't.\n\nDecisions run on the numbers. Reviews and planning work from the org's single source of truth instead of side spreadsheets, and follow-ups actually close.\n\nThe org feels coherent. People know what they're working on, why it's the priority, and how it connects to the rest of the company.\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU BRING\n\n10+ years of operating experience, with real time inside a marketing org in a Chief of Staff, business operations, or senior program-operations seat.\n\nA practitioner's understanding of demand generation and account-based marketing in a B2B context. You can talk pipeline, not just plans.\n\nComfort with marketing and pipeline metrics and with running a budget. You can build the model and read the dashboard.\n\nA track record of bringing order to a fast, complex org without grinding it to a halt.\n\nClear writing, straight talk, and the presence to hold a room of senior people to a plan.\n\n\n\nBACKGROUNDS WE'D BE EXCITED ABOUT\n\nChief of Staff or business operations at a high-growth B2B software or AI company.\n\nA marketing ops or RevOps leader who wants an org-level operating seat rather than a systems seat.\n\nStrategy or management consulting followed by an in-house operating role.\n\nA demand-gen or integrated-marketing operator who has moved into an org-level operating seat.\n\nCohere is committed to fair and transparent pay practices. You'll own that integrations surface end to end.\n\nIt’s a dual mandate: own the integrations themselves (prioritize, ship, and drive adoption) and build the underlying platform capabilities they depend on when those don't yet exist.\n\n\n\n\nOUTCOMES\n\n - Family of integrations that are adopted and driving customer value, measured by usage and retention.\n\n - Reusable, platform-level capabilities and a developer and partner on-ramp that scale across use cases.\n\n\n\n\nRESPONSIBILITIES\n\n - Define the integration ecosystem strategy for North - roadmap, catalogue priorities, and partner posture - anchored to customer demand and revenue.\n\n - Own North's integrations end to end, and partner with strategic customers to define transformative, integrations-based workflows.\n\n - Derive generic, platform-level capabilities (connector framework, auth and identity, tool-use, data sync, permissioning) where they don't yet exist, partnering with the core-experience team on shared work.\n\n - Collaborate with forward-deployed engineering to define how to evolve integration work into reusable product, to scope, sequence, and build it.\n\n - Define the developer and partner experience (APIs, SDKs, plugin model, docs) and instrument analytics to track adoption, time-to-stand-up, and retention.\n\n\n\n\nREQUIREMENTS\n\n - 5+ years in product management on platform / API, integrations, or developer / ecosystem products.\n\n - Track record shipping integration, connector, or platform products with real impact on adoption, expansion, or retention.\n\n - Experience working directly with high-stakes customers and ecosystem partners.\n\n - Technical fluency with APIs, auth, data models, and integration architecture; comfortable with first-party vs. partner vs. self-serve tradeoffs.\n\n - Analytical and metrics-first, and a strong cross-functional collaborator across engineering, design, and field / deployment teams.\n\n - Experience with AI-first product management.\n\n - Bias for shipping and iterating.\n\n - Experience with a least a few domains of: Agentic AI, LLMs, Automation, Productivity, Enterprise security and compliance.\n\n\n\n\nFULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:\n\n - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.\n\n - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.\n\n - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.\n\n - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.\n\n - Annual enrichment benefits:\n   \n   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.\n   \n   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.\n\n - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)\n\n - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.\n\n\n\n\nHOW AND WHERE WE WORK:\n\n - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.\n\n - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.\n\n - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.\n\n - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.\n   \n   \n\nIf any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. \n\n\nWe strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; Cohere’s TPMs are often described by their stakeholders as organized, execution-oriented, pragmatic, and adaptable to the needs of the company and the programs they lead.\n\nAs a reward for the depth and breadth of expertize that you bring to the table, you will get to work alongside some of the most talented engineers in the world on building cutting edge AI technology. Lead the end-to-end coordination and execution across the program, with a particular focus on cross-functional collaboration with Modeling and customer-facing teams\n\n - Identify pain points and establish processes to ensure that the team can focus on development, while meeting needs of internal and external users of the models, and improving engineering best practices\n\n - Build a strong culture around continuous improvement, such as liaising with incident management leads, ensuring that problems are accurately root caused, and that required fixes are provided in a timely manner\n\n - Manage various overlapping projects and programs, ruthlessly prioritizing asks, to ensure that the company’s top priorities are met\n\n - Collaborate with stakeholders across the company to set, track, and manage timelines, deliverables, budgets, and scope to ensure successful program execution\n\n - Deliver clear, timely, and consistent updates across engineering, leadership, and non–technical teams on the progress, plans, and incidents\n\n - Act as a strong tactical and strategic partner to the senior leads across your program, whether that be providing low-level tactical support or help answer high-level strategic problems that drives impact at the company-level.\n\n\n\n\nYOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE:\n\n5+ years of Technical Program Management experience focusing on Machine Learning Infrastructure, specifically covering areas such as model inference, serving, efficiency, and endpoints design & implementation\n\n - Experience working in a chaotic, fast paced, low structure environment. We need an EPM who is pragmatic, can roll up their sleeves when needed, and can function at the tactical and strategic level to do whatever it takes to make Cohere’s models succeed\n\n - (optional, but strongly preferred) Have technical experience in a hands-on capacity. We don’t necessarily need someone who has been working hands-on in a technical role, but the programs are inherently extremely technical. This role owns the integration pipeline end-to-end: adding new integrations to the platform, helping other engineers do the same, and becoming the owner of the process that makes that repeatable. You will also create the evals and tests that make sure those integrations work as expected and keep working as the platform evolves.\n\n\nIn this role, you will:\n\n - Build new integrations (tools) on the North agentic platform, and maintain the ones already in production.\n\n - Own the integration pipeline: the process for adding a new tool, from design to shipping to ongoing maintenance.\n\n - Help other engineers add integrations of their own, and raise the bar for how the team does it.\n\n - Create evals and tests to make sure integrations work as expected and alert on regressions.\n\n - Tune tool descriptions to improve performance based on feedback and evals.\n\n - Use AI actively in your work, while staying accountable for the quality and reliability of what you ship.\n\n\n\nYou may be a good fit if:\n\n - You have shipped production code and are comfortable building integrations against external APIs.\n\n - You have a background in evaluating agentic systems (ideal), or at minimum know what an eval is and are comfortable with prompt engineering and tool-description tuning.\n\n - You excel in fast-paced environments and can execute while priorities are a moving target.\n\n - You bring high agency: you learn quickly and drive change without waiting for perfect instructions.\n\n - You've owned things end-to-end before and care about the quality of what ships, not just that it shipped.\n\n - You enjoy helping other engineers succeed, not just shipping your own work.\n\n\n\nWorking Location:\n\nThis role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.\n\nCompensation:\n\n - For candidates based in California, New York and Washington States, the compensation range is: $180,000 – $225,000\n\n - For candidates based elsewhere in the US, the compensation range is: $150,000 – $190,000\n\n - For candidates based in Canada, the compensation range is: $215,000 – $270,000\n\n\n\n\nFULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:\n\n - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.\n\n - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.\n\n - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.\n\n - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.\n\n - Annual enrichment benefits:\n   \n   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.\n   \n   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.\n\n - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)\n\n - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.\n\n\n\n\nHOW AND WHERE WE WORK:\n\n - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.\n\n - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.\n\n - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.\n\n - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.\n   \n   \n\nIf any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. \n\n\nWe strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; Join us!\n\n\nRole Overview:\nBuilding AI agents that can assist with any kind of enterprise work is a challenging, open-ended problem. One key piece of solving it is replicating real work environments as realistically as possible - filling them with hard tasks to solve, creating plausible input data, and defining clear rewards for completing the work the right way. We build many of these reinforcement learning (RL) environments, then drop our agents into them to evaluate or train them.\n\nIn this role, you are responsible for creating these RL environments, running AI agents inside them, and improving both the agents and the environments in the process. The results reach customers, whose feedback feeds back in - and the agent/environment improvement loop continues.\n\n\nKey Responsibilities:\nThere are many open problems in this space. As a Member of Technical Staff, RL Environments, you will:\n\n - Build new RL environments targeting different agentic capabilities and industry areas\n\n - Train and evaluate agents in those environments\n\n - Make all the pieces work together: tasks, data, tool implementations, and verifiers\n\n - Work across modeling and product to identify gaps in agent performance, and improve both the agents and the environments\n\n - Work with external vendors to create high-quality, expert-built RL environments, and build tools to ensure high task, data, and verifier quality\n\n - Automate the discovery of model capability gaps, and systematically measure agent performance during evals and training\n\n\n\nQualifications:\n\nYou may be a good fit if:\n\n - You have engineered agents and optimized them for specific industry use cases\n\n - You have spent dozens of hours reviewing agent trajectories to pinpoint exact failure points and fix them with model training or harness engineering\n\n - You obsess over measuring agentic capabilities and turning that into a repeatable process\n\n - You have had many debates about what a good outcome from an AI agent should look like, you translated that into verifier implementations and tuned the reward designs\n\n - You have designed and run annotation workflows to surface insights into agent performance and verify data quality\n\n - You have built synthetic data pipelines to scale eval and training efforts\n\n - You use agents yourself in your daily work, and have stories about how you improved your setup to 10x your productivity\n\n - A plus: you have experience with training with RL: scaling, troubleshooting and tuning the environments\n\nIf some of the above doesn’t line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. \n\n\n\nWorking Location:\nThis role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. Join us!\n\n\n \n\nRole overview:\n\nNorth is Cohere’s AI workspace platform for enterprises: a secure, customizable environment where companies can use AI across their real workflows while maintaining control over sensitive data. North connects AI agents with workplace tools, applications, and business context, helping users delegate complex work, build automations, inspect outputs, and collaborate with AI in production environments.\n\n\n\nAs North becomes more capable, one of the most important questions is also one of the hardest: how do we know whether the model is actually getting better for the workflows customers care about?\n\n\n\nThis role is about being the voice of North inside modelling. You will build the evaluation systems, feedback loops, and applied modelling workflows that make sure model progress translates into better product outcomes for North users. You will work closely with North product teams, customer-facing teams, and modelling teams to define what “good” means across the product surface, turn real usage and product direction into high-quality evals, and use those evals to guide model selection, patches, and regular model updates.\n\n\n\nThis is neither a pure research role nor a conventional product engineering role. It is a rigorous applied MLE role for someone who cares deeply about measurement, model behavior, and real-world product quality. You should be excited by the craft of building careful evals: evals that capture messy agentic workflows, reflect actual customer needs, resist superficial benchmark hacking, and provide useful signal for where the product and models need to go next.\n\n\nPlease note: this team works closely across Europe and East Coast North America time zones. We are open to candidates who can collaborate effectively within those hours.\n\n\n\nKey responsibilities:\n\n - Own the eval strategy for North: define what we need to measure across agent workflows, tool use, enterprise knowledge work such as deep research, document creation or editing, and other human-AI interactions.\n\n - Build high-quality evals from the realities of the product: user feedback, production failures, privacy-preserving usage logs, internal dogfooding, customer needs, and forward-looking product goals.\n\n - Create systems that continuously turn what North is learning from users, customers, and feature teams into evals, so measurement keeps pace with the product rather than becoming a static benchmark.\n\n - Be the voice of North inside modelling: extract clear insight from eval results, customer-derived data and product context, then turn model failures, capability gaps, and North-specific needs into actionable recommendations for the central modelling teams.\n   \n\nQualifications:\n\n - You have improved LLM-powered, agent-powered, or AI-product systems through evals, feedback loops, data curation, prompting, model adaptation, or model selection.\n\n - You care deeply about evaluation as a craft: representative tasks, precise rubrics, clean data, failure analysis, regression tracking, and knowing when a metric is giving false confidence.\n\n - You have strong applied MLE judgment and can reason clearly about model behavior, eval validity, product outcomes, and production tradeoffs.\n\n - You are comfortable working close to users and product teams, while translating messy qualitative signals into measurement that other modelling teams can act on.\n\n - You are self-directed, practical, and motivated by open-ended problems where the right answer requires both technical depth and product understanding.\n\n - You care about making AI systems genuinely useful in real enterprise settings, not just better on abstract benchmarks.\n\n\n\nIf some of the above does not line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.\n\n\n\nWorking Location:\nThis role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description -
